stage: board: the fully quantised W8A8 model (1 layer) now produces the CORRECT result on FPGA5

root_cause.symptom: the board produced a logit of 802603 (about 91000x too large) and every activation scale read back as a denormal or NaN, while the identical graph in the host JIT matched the reference exactly
root_cause.cause: the generated bare-metal main passed an extra cache-position descriptor. The graph's inputs are [ids, position, K0, V0, position1, K1, V1, ...] -- layer 0 uses the TOP-LEVEL position and only later layers carry their own. My generator emitted a position for layer 0 as well, so every argument after it was bound one slot to the right and the kernels wrote into each other's buffers.
root_cause.why_the_earlier_evidence_looked_like_a_k: uninitialized DDR reads back as denormals and NaNs, which is exactly what a mis-bound workspace looks like; the kernels themselves were fine, as the 72-case board suite already showed.
root_cause.how_it_was_found: printing the activation scale of every linear in graph order bracketed it: after the fix they read 3D84DD8A (0.0648), 3C8D5CC2 (0.0173), 3D55C518 (0.0522), 3EC902B1 (0.3926) -- all plausible per-row scales -- where before they were denormals.
root_cause.arity_check_that_confirms_the_fix: the entry takes 60 arguments: 1 results pointer + 22 parameters + 4 graph inputs + 33 workspace buffers. The generated call passes exactly those.

not_done: the 28-layer image has not been re-linked with this fix, and even then it needs a multi-hour board window (attention alone measured at about 51 minutes)
